key_insight: RoSHI fuses low-cost sparse IMUs with egocentric Project Aria glasses to recover full 3D human pose and body shape in a metric global frame, combining portability, occlusion robustness, and global consistency in-the-wild.
problem_solved: Existing human data collection methods force trade-offs between portability, robustness to occlusion, and global metric consistency; RoSHI resolves these by hybridizing wearable IMUs and head-mounted egocentric perception for long-horizon, real-world capture.
method: Hybrid hardware: integrate sparse, low-cost IMUs on the body with Project Aria egocentric glasses to capture complementary signals.
Sensor-fusion pipeline: register and fuse egocentric visual cues and IMU measurements to estimate full 3D pose and body shape in a shared metric global coordinate frame.
Practical calibration & body-model fitting designed for long-horizon, in-the-wild data capture (lightweight and robust to occlusions).
impact: Enables scalable collection of rich, metrically-aligned human interaction data for robot learning, imitation, and human–robot interaction research—reducing reliance on constrained lab setups and improving training data realism.
visual_elements: Hardware diagram: Project Aria glasses + IMU placement map on a human silhouette (labels for sensors).
Pipeline flowchart: sensors → calibration → sensor fusion → 3D pose & shape in global frame (with brief captions).
Before/after visualization: egocentric camera frame alongside reconstructed 3D human in room-level metric coordinates (overlayed).
Comparison radar/chart: trade-offs (portability, occlusion robustness, global consistency, cost) vs prior approaches.
paper_title: RoSHI: A Versatile Robot-oriented Suit for Human Data In-the-Wild
paper_authors: Wenjing Margaret Mao, Jefferson Ng, Luyang Hu, Daniel Gehrig, Antonio Loquercio
